jobs.title: Product Manager, Growth
jobs.description:
Product Manager, Growth

What we want to accomplish and why we need you

Suki is a leading technology company that provides AI voice solutions for healthcare. Our mission is to reimagine the healthcare technology stack, making it invisible and assistive to lift the administrative burden from clinicians. Our flagship product, Suki Assistant, uses generative AI to automatically create clinical documentation by ambiently listening to patient-clinician conversations. Suki helps clinicians complete notes 72% faster on average, assists with coding and answering questions, and delivers a 9X ROI in year 1.

Clinicians that use Suki already spend over 70% less time on administrative tasks — and we're striving to do even better. Come join us!

We are a user-driven company committed to making sure every pixel of our product is in service of doctors. We're a team of technologists, clinicians, and industry experts working together to push the limits on technology in medicine. We're confident enough to move fast and talented enough not to break things.

The opportunity

Suki grows through its product — and we need someone who can measure, understand, and improve that motion with rigor. We're looking for a Product Manager, Growth with strong analytical instincts to own how clinicians activate, engage, and retain within Suki. You'll define success metrics, build measurement frameworks, run experiments, and translate data into product decisions that move the needle on adoption.

This role sits at the intersection of product and analytics. You won't just look at dashboards — you'll build them, instrument the events that feed them, design the experiments that test your hypotheses, and use the results to ship better product. You'll partner closely with Engineering, Data, Customer Success, and Sales to close the loop between data and delivery.

What you'll own

Measurement and Funnel Analysis

- Define success metrics and build measurement frameworks for clinician activation, engagement, and retention — particularly in greenfield areas where metrics aren't yet established

- Conduct deep-dive funnel analyses to understand where clinicians drop off, what drives engagement, and what distinguishes power users from churned ones

- Build and maintain dashboards and self-service analytics tools that give the broader team visibility into funnel performance and product health

- Partner with Engineering to advocate for upstream instrumentation best practices — ensuring events are captured with consistent schemas and sufficient fidelity to answer growth questions

Experimentation

- Design and execute A/B tests and phased rollouts to measure the incremental impact of product changes on activation and retention

- Define guardrails and success/failure criteria for experiments before they run, not after

- Synthesize experiment results into clear product recommendations and feed learnings back into roadmap prioritization

Product Delivery

- Translate analytical findings and clinician feedback into well-scoped product requirements that engineering teams can execute against

- Own the growth product roadmap: identify the highest-leverage bets based on data, size them, and drive them to launch

- Partner with Customer Success and Sales to surface field insights and validate them against product usage data

What we're looking for

- Analytically rigorous : You reach for data first. You know how to slice a funnel, design a clean experiment, and tell the difference between correlation and causation. SQL is a native language, not a stretch skill.

- Instrumentally curious : You care about where the data comes from. You've worked with engineering to define event taxonomies, and you've felt the pain of trying to answer a question when the tracking wasn't there.

- Builder : You don't just analyze — you use what you learn to ship. You write specs engineers love to read and you hold the product accountable to the metrics you defined.

- Action oriented : You move fast, iterate on signal, and don't wait for perfect information.

- Clinician-empathetic : You can hold a quantitative understanding of funnel behavior and a qualitative understanding of clinical workflows at the same time.

- Mission-driven : You are as passionate about reducing clinician burnout as we are.

Responsibilities

- Define, instrument, and own growth metrics across the clinician journey — from first login through power-user activation — and drive accountability to them across the team

- Conduct funnel analyses and deep-dives to identify root causes of adoption gaps and surface high-value opportunities for product improvement

- Design and execute experiments (A/B tests, holdout groups, phased rollouts) with pre-registered success criteria; synthesize results into product decisions

- Build dashboards and self-service tools that give product, CS, sales, and leadership clear visibility into clinician activation and retention

- Partner with Engineering to define event instrumentation requirements and ensure analytics foundations are experiment-ready

- Write clear, detailed product requirements that translate growth hypotheses and clinical workflow needs into shippable product

- Partner with Customer Success, Sales, and clinical SMEs to triangulate qualitative field insights with quantitative product data

Requirements

- Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field (Computer Science, Statistics, Economics, or related) and 4+ years of experience in technology, or a Master's degree with 2+ years of product management experience

- Demonstrated experience in growth or product analytics in a B2B SaaS environment — you've owned a funnel, moved a metric, and can explain precisely how

- Strong SQL fluency; comfortable pulling, slicing, and visualizing data independently without waiting for a data analyst

- Hands-on experience designing and analyzing A/B tests and other experiments; understands statistical significance, power, and common pitfalls

- Experience defining metrics and building measurement frameworks in ambiguous or greenfield environments

- Familiarity with product analytics and experimentation tools (e.g., Mixpanel, Amplitude, Statsig, Looker, or similar)

- Experience working in Agile environments and thriving in a fast-paced, startup context

- Healthcare experience or familiarity with clinical workflows is a plus; curiosity and ability to learn quickly is a must

Suki is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are dedicated to building a company that fosters inclusion and belonging and reflects the diverse communities we serve across the country. We know we are stronger this way, and we look forward to growing our team with these shared values.

In compliance with the State of California Pay Transparency Law, the base salary range for this role is between $215,000 and $245,000 in CA. This range is not inclusive of any discretionary bonus or equity package. When determining a candidate’s compensation, we consider a number of factors including skillset, experience, job scope, and current market data.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Platform Products
jobs.description:
Head of Platform Products

SD Product, Suki for Partners

Why Suki — and Why Now

Suki is creating a new category in health technology: the AI-powered digital assistant for healthcare. Our mission is simple but profound—give time back to clinicians so they can focus on what matters most: caring for patients.

Today, doctors spend hours navigating complex electronic health record (EHR) systems—modern versions of paper charts that are often unintuitive, fragmented, and time-consuming. Suki changes that. Clinicians using Suki already spend 70% less time on administrative work, and we’re just getting started.

Our platform is the foundation of everything we do. As we scale AI-powered capabilities across voice, ambient, and enterprise experiences—and extend them to health system partners, EHR ecosystems, and third-party developers—we need a seasoned platform product leader to define and drive the next generation of our technical platform strategy.

The Role

As Head of Platform Products, you will own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for Suki’s core platform—the APIs, services, and integration layers that enable external partners to build on top of our technology.

You will lead a team of platform product managers and serve as a strategic partner to Engineering, Commercial, and executive leadership. Your work will determine how Suki’s AI, speech, and clinical intelligence capabilities are architected, scaled, and delivered to the broader healthcare ecosystem.

This is a rare opportunity to shape the platform that underpins an AI-first healthcare company—and to set a new standard for how health technology platforms are built and scaled.

What You’ll Do

Define Platform Vision & Strategy

- Own and drive a clear, compelling multi-year platform product strategy that enables Suki’s product portfolio and ecosystem growth

- Define the platform’s service architecture, API strategy, and extensibility model to support current products and future innovation

- Translate complex AI/ML, NLP, and speech capabilities into well-architected, reusable platform services

Drive Interoperability & Health Data Strategy

- Own the strategy for integrations including EHR (Athena and others), ensuring deep, reliable, and scalable connectivity

- Define the approach to health data standards (FHIR, HL7, CDA) and ensure the platform is built for healthcare-grade interoperability

- Partner with compliance and security teams to maintain HIPAA compliance, SOC 2 certification, and enterprise-grade data governance across the platform

Scale AI & ML Platform Capabilities

- Work closely with AI/ML leadership to productize core capabilities—ambient AI, clinical NLP, medical speech recognition, and generative AI—as scalable platform services

- Enable rapid experimentation and deployment of new AI capabilities across product surfaces

Build for the Ecosystem

- Define and execute the developer platform and partner integration strategy, including APIs, SDKs, documentation, and developer experience

- Work with business development and partnerships teams to identify and enable high-value platform use cases for health systems, EHR vendors, and third-party developers

- Build the foundation for a platform ecosystem that creates compounding value for Suki and its partners

Be a Strategic Product Partner

- Partner closely with the Chief Product Officer, Engineering leadership, and Commercial leadership to align platform investments with company strategy and product roadmap

- Ground platform decisions in data, customer insights, technical feasibility, and business impact

- Drive prioritization and trade-off decisions across competing platform demands from internal teams and external partners

Build and Scale a World-Class Team

- Lead, mentor, and grow a high-performing platform product management team

- Foster a culture of technical excellence, customer empathy, accountability, and impact

- Identify and close gaps in skills, tools, processes, and operating models as the platform organization scales

What We’re Looking For

- 12+ years of product management experience, with 5+ years in senior/leadership roles owning platform, infrastructure, or developer-facing products

- Deep expertise in platform product management: APIs, developer experience, data platforms, integration architectures, and service-oriented systems

- Strong background in healthcare technology, with hands-on experience navigating EHR ecosystems, health data standards (FHIR, HL7), and regulatory requirements (HIPAA, SOC 2)

- Experience productizing AI/ML capabilities at scale—ideally in NLP, speech, or applied clinical AI

- Proven track record of building and scaling platform product teams in high-growth, product-led organizations

- Technically fluent: comfortable engaging deeply with engineering and data science teams on architecture, systems design, and technical trade-offs

- Strong analytical and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to balance long-term platform bets with near-term product delivery

- Excellent executive communication skills—able to articulate platform value and strategy to technical and non-technical stakeholders alike

- Experience with enterprise SaaS and multi-tenant platform architectures is strongly preferred

- Bay Area–based is ideal, but not required

Tell me more about Suki

- On a roll: Named by Fast Company as the Next Big Thing in Tech, by Comparably for the Best Leadership Team, by Frost & Sullivan for a Technology Innovation Leadership award, just to name a few.

- Great team: Founded, managed, and backed by successful tech veterans from Google and Apple and medical leaders from UCSF and Stanford. We have technologists and doctors working side-by-side to solve complex problems.

- Great investors: We’re backed by Venrock, First Round Capital, Flare Capital, March Capital, Hedosophia and others. With our $165M raised so far, we have the resources to scale.

- Huge market: Disrupting a massive, growing $30+ billion market for transcription, dictation, and order-entry solutions. Our vision is to become the voice user interface for healthcare, relieving the administrative burden on doctors instead of adding to it.

- Great customers: Our solutions are used in health systems and clinics across the country, supporting clinicians across dozens of specialties.  Check out what one of our users says about how Suki has given her a sense of balance.

- Impact: You’ll make an impact from day one. You’ll join a team working towards a shared purpose with a culture built upon deep empathy for doctors and passion for making their lives better.

Suki is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are dedicated to building a company that fosters inclusion and belonging and reflects the diverse communities we serve across the country. We know we are stronger this way and we look forward to growing our team with these shared values.

In compliance with the State of California Pay Transparency Law, the base salary range for this role is between $300k to $350k in CA. This range is not inclusive of any discretionary bonus or equity package. When determining a candidate’s compensation, we consider a number of factors including skillset, experience, job scope, and current market data.

What we want to accomplish and why we need you

Suki is a leading technology company that provides AI voice solutions for healthcare. We’re confident enough to move fast and talented enough not to break things.

About the role

We're growing our Engineering Operations function and looking for a Technical Program Manager to embed directly in an engineering pod and make execution predictable, measurable, and fast. You'll own your pod's day-to-day execution, give leadership an accurate picture of where things stand, and help scale the operating model that makes execution repeatable across the engineering organization. A hands-on role for someone who likes both running the machine and improving how it runs.

What you'll do

- Own execution for your pod: run sprint planning, stand-ups, reviews, and retrospectives, partnering closely with Product and Engineering leads.

- Keep the pod's work tracked and trustworthy, so status rolls up accurately from task to program level.

- Produce clear, regular status reporting for pod leads and senior leadership, surfacing risks early.

- Own the metrics that matter: delivery predictability, sprint coverage, spillover, backlog health, and cycle time.

- Drive spec-driven development — ensure work is well-specified before build, and measure and improve time from signed-off spec to shipped code.

- Champion process, tooling, and AI-assisted productivity improvements, feeding durable wins back into the broader operating model.

What you'll gain

- Applied clinical AI fluency — work at the center of an ACI platform spanning ASR, NLP, LLMs, and deep EHR integration, and learn how a real production AI system ships.

- Systems-level judgment — build a rare, end-to-end mental model of how complex software gets built, from spec to production, across Product, Engineering, ML, and QA.

- Data and metrics craft — own the instrumentation and dashboards leadership runs on.

- Process architecture — help design the operating model that scales across the org, not just run an existing playbook.

- Executive-grade influence — regular exposure to senior leadership and the reps to turn ambiguity into decision-ready narratives.

What we're looking for

- 3–5 years as a Technical Program Manager driving delivery for software engineering teams.

- Technical fluency to navigate the work :
- Reads and reasons about system architecture — services, APIs, and how frontend, backend, and ML components fit together.
- Understands the full software development lifecycle: specs, code review, CI/CD, testing/QA, release, and monitoring.
- Grounded enough in ML/AI systems to follow conversations about models, data pipelines, evaluation, and what separates a demo from production.
- Reads a design doc or PRD, asks sharp questions, and spots gaps, assumptions, and risks.

- Data and metrics craft: fluent with issue-tracking tools (e.g. Jira), keeps a clean backlog as a single source of truth, and drives improvement with data.

- Excellent written communication: turns messy execution reality into crisp updates for engineers and executives alike, and builds trust fast with Product, Engineering, and Design.

- Sound judgment and autonomy: thrives in a fast-moving environment, escalates through the right channels, and knows when to standardize versus adapt.

- Great team: Founded, managed, and backed by successful tech veterans from Google and Apple and medical leaders from UCSF and Stanford. We have technologists and doctors working side-by-side to solve complex problems.

- Great investors: We’re backed by Venrock, First Round Capital, Flare Capital, March Capital, Hedosophia and others. With our $165M raised so far, we have the resources to scale.

- Huge market: Disrupting a massive, growing $30+ billion market for transcription, dictation, and order-entry solutions. Our vision is to become the voice user interface for healthcare, relieving the administrative burden on doctors instead of adding to it.

- Great customers: Our solutions are used in health systems and clinics across the country, supporting clinicians across dozens of specialties.  Check out what one of our users says about how Suki has helped his practice.

- Impact: You’ll make an impact from day one. You’ll join a team working towards a shared purpose with a culture built upon deep empathy for doctors and passion for making their lives better.

Suki is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are dedicated to building a company that fosters inclusion and belonging and reflects the diverse communities we serve across the country. We know we are stronger this way, and we look forward to growing our team with these shared values.
